messages:
marie-support: Hey team — ACME reported repeated 500s + huge token latency on their Dedicated EU cluster around 2025-10-12 01:02-01:10 UTC. Customer provided request_id=rcq-9f2b7 and says response stalled after ~12s. They attached a curl they used. Can we collect repro steps, k8s logs, GPU metrics, and a debug bundle?

marie-support: curl they ran:
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXX' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"rw-large-1","input":"Summarize this...","max_tokens":1024}'
```

devon-sre: Got it. First ask: which Dedicated cluster? Customer says eu-west-2-ded. Can you confirm pod names and the node IPs? Also capture kubectl logs for container runtime and sidecar, and `kubectl describe` for pods to check OOM/killed events.

marie-support: Confirmed cluster eu-west-2-ded. Active inference pods during window: inf-serve-0-5ff8c, inf-serve-1-7d2b1, cache-proxy-0. Node IPs: 10.12.34.5 (gpu-a), 10.12.34.6 (gpu-b). No churn reported by customer.

alexa-eng-runtime: Thanks. Steps I'd collect locally (quick list):
- kubectl -n dedicated logs inf-serve-0-5ff8c -c runtime --since=20m > /tmp/inf-0-runtime.log
- kubectl -n dedicated logs inf-serve-0-5ff8c -c sidecar --since=20m > /tmp/inf-0-sidecar.log
- kubectl -n dedicated describe pod inf-serve-0-5ff8c > /tmp/inf-0-describe.txt
- on node 10.12.34.5 run `sudo dmesg | tail -n 200` and `sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2025-10-12 00:50" --until "2025-10-12 01:20"`
- nvidia-smi snapshot during window: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,timestamp,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/nvshot.csv` (or grab from our GPU exporter)

devon-sre: Also collect our runtime trace ids: check /var/log/redwood/runtime-trace.log for lines matching rcq-9f2b7 or lookups for correlation_id in request logs. If there's a backend 5xx we want the stacktrace from runtime service.

marie-support: I'm on it — grabbing logs now. Pasting top-level runtime error snippets I found in inf-serve-0 logs around 01:04 UTC:
```
2025-10-12T01:04:11.342Z ERROR RequestHandler request_id=rcq-9f2b7 status=500 "runtime: kv-cache miss + kernel timeout"
2025-10-12T01:04:11.344Z ERROR stacktrace: runtime/panic at runtime/gpu_cache.go:128
2025-10-12T01:04:11.345Z INFO routing: selected model variant rw-large-1-q8
```

alexa-eng-runtime: Interesting — it picked a quantized variant (rw-large-1-q8) via routing policy. Quantized kernels can hit edge-case kernels on certain driver combos. Please also collect the kernel module versions: `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` and `nvidia-smi -q | grep 'Driver Version' -A1`.

marie-support: Collected nvidia-smi snapshot and driver info from gpu-a (10.12.34.5):
```
Driver Version                     : 470.199.02
Timestamp, index, utilization.gpu [%], utilization.memory [%], memory.used [MiB]
2025-10-12T01:03:59, 0, 93, 40, 11445
2025-10-12T01:04:00, 0, 98, 44, 11470
2025-10-12T01:04:01, 0, 99, 45, 11474
```

devon-sre: High GPU util at that time. Any kernel OOM or GPU reset in dmesg?

marie-support: dmesg shows a GPU fault around the same time: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=3456`. No full node reboot. kubelet logs show transient network timeout to model cache store: `Get https://10.12.34.20:8080/cache/kv failed: context deadline exceeded`. That matches the runtime error about kv-cache miss + kernel timeout.

alexa-eng-runtime: For repro, we should reproduce the request with same headers + body but force selection of the q8 variant. Repro curl (use our internal routing header to pin variant):
```bash
curl -X POST https://dedicated-eu.redwood.internal/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXX' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Routing: variant=rw-large-1-q8' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-1","input":"repeat token-heavy prompt...","max_tokens":1024}' -v
```

marie-support: I'm preparing a debug bundle now. Commands I ran to collect files:
- tar cvzf debug-bundle-1768504321-acme.tar.gz /var/log/redwood/runtime-trace.log /tmp/inf-*-runtime.log /tmp/inf-*-sidecar.log /tmp/inf-*-describe.txt /tmp/nvshot.csv /var/log/kubelet.log /var/log/syslog
- uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/eu/debug-bundles/debug-bundle-1768504321-acme.tar.gz

ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary deploy rw-large-1-q8 started 2025-10-12T00:55:00Z -> 2025-10-12T01:05:00Z, rollout_percentage=20% :information_source:

devon-sre: That canary overlaps the window. Possibly variant had a kernel regression on driver 470.199.02. Next steps:
- Share debug-bundle link with eng-runtime + infra.
- If eng-runtime repros locally, capture `strace` of runtime process when we see 500.
- Infra to check GPU driver upgrade history on eu nodes and confirm whether runner image has custom cuda libs.

alexa-eng-runtime: I'll try to repro on staging pinned to the same driver + variant. If I can reproduce, I'll capture the full stacktrace and a minimal reproducer to send to kernel/driver team. Also add a temporary routing rule to avoid rw-large-1-q8 for this customer.

marie-support: Uploaded bundle: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-debug/eu/debug-bundles/debug-bundle-1768504321-acme.tar.gz 

devon-sre: Thanks. Marking RCA path: likely q8 kernel edge-case + kv-cache network timeout. Assigning owners: @alexa-eng-runtime to validate repro + stacktrace, @devon-sre to verify infra/driver, @marie-support to coordinate customer comms and temporary routing workaround.

marie-support: Noted — I'll tell ACME we have the bundle and a mitigation: pin to non-q8 variant for now and schedule a follow-up once eng/runtime confirms. :thumbsup:

alexa-eng-runtime: I'll post updates here after repro attempts. If I can reproduce, will include a short curl-based minimal repro and the exact strace/stack.

devon-sre: One more capture action: run `kubectl top pod` around repro to capture pod-level CPU/memory, and `kubectl get events --namespace dedicated --since=30m` to surface kube-scheduler evictions.

marie-support: Copy that. Closing thread when eng/runtime confirms repro or we have a patch plan.
